short: The Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact is a self-regulatory initiative launched in January 2021 by European data center operators and trade associations, committing signatories to climate-neutral data centers by 2030 through PUE, clean energy, water, circular economy and heat targets; it is not a law, and its certification is voluntary.
title: Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact
subtitle: A self-regulatory initiative of European data center operators and trade associations to reach climate neutrality by 2030
body_html:
What the Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact is

The Climate Neutral Data Centre Pact is a self-regulatory initiative of data center operators and trade associations in Europe. It was launched on 21 January 2021 with 25 operators and 17 trade associations, and its signatories commit to making data centers climate neutral by 2030. The Pact's governance document says it was created by two trade associations, CISPE (Cloud Infrastructure Service Providers in Europe) and the EUDCA (European Data Centre Association), to agree environmental targets for data centers operating in Europe and to coordinate with the European Union.

What it covers

The Initiative text sets targets in five areas:

  • Energy efficiency: new data centers at full capacity meet an annual PUE of 1.3 in cool climates and 1.4 in warm climates by 1 January 2025; existing data centers meet the same targets by 1 January 2030. The targets apply to data centers above 50 kW of maximum IT power, with PUE measured under ISO/IEC 30134-2 or EN 50600-4-2.
  • Clean energy: electricity demand matched by 75% renewable energy or hourly carbon-free energy by 31 December 2025, and 100% by 31 December 2030.
  • Water: from 1 January 2025, new data centers at full capacity in cool climates that use potable water are designed to a maximum WUE of 0.4 litres per kWh in water-stressed areas, adjusted for climate, water stress and water type. Existing data centers that replace a cooling system must meet the new-build target by 31 December 2040.
  • Circular economy: operators assess 100% of used server equipment for reuse, repair or recycling, and set a target percentage for repair and reuse.
  • Circular energy systems: operators explore connecting new data centers to district heating and other heat users where that is practical, environmentally sound and cost effective.

How a claim is made and checked

Operators and trade associations join by signing a pledge to the Initiative's targets. Signed members may display the Pact logo to show commitment. The Pact website keeps a public list of members.

Certification under the Pact is voluntary. Operators that certify their adherence under the Pact's control framework receive a logo marked "certified" with the year, valid for three years. The site's timeline records an auditable framework presented to the European Commission in December 2022, first signatories certifying compliance in March 2023, and results of two certification rounds presented to the Commission in July 2023 and October 2024. The site says that from 2025 members no longer perform separate self-audits but use mandatory reporting under EU legislation to show progress toward 2030. The governance document says EU law reporting with similar controls counts toward the Pact's certification.

The Pact's board may vote to remove an operator that is not following data center specific EU regulation or is not showing suitable commitment to the targets, after a written explanation and a 30-day appeal period.

What a claim does not mean

  • The Pact is not a law and not a regulator. It is a voluntary self-regulatory commitment by industry.
  • Signing the Pact is a pledge to meet targets by the stated dates, not proof that a data center meets them now.
  • A "certified" Pact logo is the Pact's own voluntary certification, valid three years, not an accredited third-party certificate.
  • The membership of a trade association does not make each of its member companies a Pact Operator.
  • The targets apply per data center with definitions (cool and warm climate, full capacity 24 months after operation begins, up to 10% of sites exempt under a utilisation rule), so a headline PUE figure needs those definitions to be read correctly.

In data centers

Membership is held by a company or trade association, not a facility. The Initiative asks operators to set out their own data center footprint and how each facility meets the targets. A reader should check the company is on the Pact's member list as an operator, whether it holds the "certified" logo and for which year, and whether it publishes per-site PUE, renewable or carbon-free energy share and WUE. For clean energy, the Initiative allows measurement at facility, country or company portfolio level, so a 100% claim may be portfolio-wide.

Related standards

The Pact measures PUE and renewable energy with the KPI parts of EN 50600 and ISO/IEC 30134. See also the EU Code of Conduct for Data Centres and ISO 50001.
